<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Isaía Prophéta
<r>Isa 43:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Et nunc hæc dicit Dóminus creans te Iacob, et formans te Israël: Noli timére, quia redémi te, et vocávi te nómine tuo: meus es tu.
<n>2</n> Cum transíeris per aquas, tecum ero, et flúmina non opérient te: cum ambuláveris in igne, non comburéris, et flamma non ardébit in te.
<n>3</n> Quia ego Dóminus Deus tuus sanctus Israël salvátor tuus, dedi propitiatiónem tuam Ægýptum, Æthiópiam, et Saba pro te.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Ecce apparébit Dóminus super nubem cándidam, et cum eo Sanctórum míllia: et habébit in vestiménto, et in fémore suo scriptum:
* Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium.
<r>℣.</r> Apparébit in finem, et non mentiétur; si moram fécerit, exspécta eum, quia véniens véniet.
<r>℟.</r> Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium.

b.0d5c0e45a8:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>extodécimo Kaléndas Ianuárii Luna undevicésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ natális sancti Ioánnis de Matha, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Ordinis sanctíssimæ Trinitátis redemptiónis captivórum Fundátor éxstitit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas, ex dispositióne Innocéntii Papæ Undécimi, ágitur sexto Idus Februárii.
<h>M</h>assíliæ, in Gállia, beáti Lázari Epíscopi, sanctárum Maríæ Magdalénæ ac Marthæ fratris, quem Dóminus in Evangélio appellásse amícum et a mórtuis excitásse légitur.
<h>E</h>leutherópoli, in Palæstína, sanctórum Mártyrum Floriáni, Calaníci, et Sociórum quinquagínta et octo; qui, témpore Heráclii Imperatóris, a Saracénis ob Christi fidem occísi sunt.
<h>I</h>n monastério Fuldénsi sancti Stúrmii, Abbátis et Saxóniæ Apóstoli; quem Innocéntius Papa Secúndus, in Concílio secúndo Lateranénsi, in Sanctórum númerum rétulit.
<h>B</h>igárdis, prope Bruxéllas, in Brabántia, sanctæ Wivínæ Vírginis, cuius egrégiam sanctitátem mirácula crebra testántur.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sanctæ Olympíadis Víduæ.
<h>A</h>ndániæ, apud Septem Ecclésias, in Bélgio, beátæ Beggæ Víduæ, quæ fuit soror sanctæ Gertrúdis.
<h>E</h>ódem die Translátio sancti Ignátii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, tértius post beátum Petrum Apóstolum, Antiochénam rexit Ecclésiam. Eius corpus ab urbe Roma, ubi ipse, sub Traiáno, glorióse martýrium tertiodécimo Kaléndas Ianuárii consummáverat, Antiochíam delátum, ibídem, in cœmetério Ecclésiæ, extra portam Daphníticam, pósitum fuit; in qua celebritáte sanctus Ioánnes Chrysóstomus conciónem ad pópulum hábuit. Póstmodum vero eius relíquiæ rursus Romam translátæ sunt, et in Ecclésia sancti Cleméntis, una cum córpore eiúsdem beatíssimi Papæ et Mártyris, summa veneratióne recónditæ.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.6004fc480f:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 17th 2027, the 19th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, holy John de la Matha, founder of the Order of the most Holy Trinity for the redemption of captives. (He died in the year 1213.) His feast is kept upon the 8th day of February by order of Innocent XI.
<h>A</h>t Marseilles, in Gaul, blessed Lazarus, (called first) Bishop (of that city,) of whom it is written in the Gospel that the Lord raised him from the dead.
<h>A</h>t Eleutheropolis, in Palestine, the holy martyrs Florian, Calanicus, and fifty-eight others, their Companions, who were slain by the Saracens for Christ's faith's sake in the time of the Emperor Heraclius.
<h>I</h>n the monastery of Fulda, (in the year 779,) the holy Abbot Sturmius, (of the Order of St Benedict, and first Abbot of Fulda,) Apostle of Saxony, whose name Innocent II enrolled with those of the saints at the second Council of Lateran.
<h>A</h>t Groot-Bijgaarden, near Brussels, in the Brabant, (in the year 1168,) the holy Virgin Wivina, whose eminent holiness is oftentimes attested by miracles. (Foundress of the Abbey of Bijgaarden, in the Archdiocese of Mechelen, of the Order of St. Benedict.)
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy widow Olympias, (about the year 410; born about 368.)
<h>I</h>n the Ardennes, the blessed Widow Begga, sister of holy Gertrude. (She married Ansegise, son of St. Arnoult, Bishop of Metz. She was born about 368, became a widow in 386, and died about 410.)
<h>U</h>pon the same day is commemorated the translation of the body of the holy martyr Ignatius, Patriarch of Antioch, who was the third to govern that church after the blessed Apostle Peter he suffered at Rome under Trajan, but his body was brought thence to Antioch and laid in the cemetery of the church outside the gate which leadeth unto Daphne, upon the anniversary of the which ceremony holy John Chrysostom preached unto the people. In after-times the body was again brought back to Rome, where it is buried, and highly honoured in the church of St. Clement along with the body of that most blessed Pope and martyr.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
